steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Representation in film refers to the ways in which different social groups, identities and experiences are constructed, depicted and made meaningful on screen. | Key Fact: Gender representation in Hollywood has historically prioritised male protagonists and marginalised female characters into limited roles such as the damsel, the love interest or the mother figure. | Key Fact: The Bechdel Test highlights the minimal representation of women in film by asking whether a film features two named women who talk to each other about something other than a man. | Key Fact: Laura Mulvey's concept of the male gaze argues that Hollywood cinema positions women as objects of visual pleasure for a presumed heterosexual male viewer, fragmenting the female body through camera work.
